newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, October 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, October 9.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Pds leader Massimo D'Alema is optimistic: "an agreement is possible" for the all-party bi-cameral commission which should carry out constitutional reforms (all).

* As the Constitutional Court ruled it is illegal to reiterate decree-laws, the parliament has little time to convert into laws 55 expiring decrees. Post and communications minister Antonio Maccanico says the majority should find an agreement with the opposition, otherwise the parliament will choke up (Corriere della Sera).
* Doctors say the Pope is not suffering from a tumour and might be back on his feet today after the operation to remove is appendix (all).
* A Russian cargo plane crashed in a village near Turin killing four people and wounding 15 (all).
* Trade unions ask the government to intervene in the dispute with employers over the renewal of metalworkers contract (Corriere).
* Carmaker Fiat plans to invest 1.5 trillion lire in India over the next 5 years (Sole 24 Ore, La Stampa).

* Japanese companies Sony and Nec are said to be interested in Olivetti's ailing pc division, as Olivetti director of policy and strategy for the telecom business Tommaso Pompei resigned (Sole 24 Ore).
* The Treasury is expected to call an auction by December 20 for the sale of 60 per cent of troubled Banco di Napoli (Sole 24 Ore).
* Italy had a trade surplus of 40.526 trillion lire in the first seven months of 1996 (Sole 24 Ore).
* In an interview Pds leader Massimo D'Alema says the government might pass a decree setting up a telecom Authority to speed up the privatisation of Stet (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
